title: Per-route degradable SLI schema, warm-standby failover and circuit-breaker escalation playbook
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Goal: Provide an operational playbook and machine-readable schema for per-route SLIs that explicitly support graceful degradation, a warm-standby regional failover mode, and a clear circuit-breaker escalation ladder. This ticket captures definitions, thresholds, automated remediation actions, observability hooks, and an implementation checklist. Motivation: our existing SLI/SLO artifacts focus on single-region availability and tail latency; we need a structured approach to declare degradable quality for conversational and reranking routes that tolerate controlled quality trade-offs during regional strain. The playbook must be consumable by routing automation (e.g., Arbiters) and by on-call runbooks.
slis: Request success rate (5xx and 4xx-without-retry) per route: numerator = successful responses with final code <500 and not application-level rejection, denominator = total requests. Window: 30m and 7d.
Latency P50/P95/P99 measured at model response emission (post-decode start) per route. Window: 5m for alerting, 7d for SLOs.
Tail-quality SLI (acceptance rate against route promptset): percentage of responses that pass automated promptset validator. Window: daily rolling 14d.
KV-cache hit rate per route and per model variant (for stateful chat): percent of requests served with hot cache. Window: 1h and 24h.
Cold-start frequency: percent of requests requiring cold kernel initialization on GPU for that route. Window: 24h.
Graceful-fallback success: percent of requests that successfully fall back to pinned smaller variant when primary variant is unavailable. Window: 1d.
slo_policy: Primary SLOs are declared per-route and per-variant. Example: /v1/chat/generate (conversational-large): availability >= 99.5 (30d), p95 latency <= 650ms (30d), tail-quality >= 99.0 (30d).

Degradable SLO bands: routes may declare tiered SLOs (Gold/Silver/Bronze) representing progressively relaxed latency/quality thresholds with pre-declared eviction credit. Eviction credit budgets are assigned to each band and encoded in the SLO manifest.
Error budget accounting: 30d rolling windows used for consumer-facing SLOs; 7d short-term window for burn-rate detection and automated remediation policies.
SLO change policy: changes to an SLO manifest require +1 reliability review and a canary deployment gating (see rollout_checklist).
error_budget_handling: Burn-rate monitoring: when 7d burn rate > 8x expected, trigger immediate mitigation path A; if >16x, escalate to path B.
Path A (soft): enable prioritized batching and increase KV-cache TTL priming for affected routes, open low-priority request queue for non-interactive calls, notify owners.
Path B (hard): engage circuit-breaker tier 2 (see circuit_breaker_matrix) which will preemptively reject Bronze-tier routes and route traffic to warm-standby regions for Gold/Silver routes.
Error budget borrowing: cross-route borrowing allowed only with explicit ledger entry and manual approval; automated borrowing disabled by default.
Post-incident remediation: any event that consumes >25% of a route's 30d budget triggers a retrospective and temporary SLO tightening to prevent thrash.
Escalation timeline: detection -> 2m to apply soft mitigations -> 10m to evaluate -> 30m to engage hard mitigations if burn persists.
warm_standby_design: Concept: warm-standby regions run minimal compatible model variants with pre-warmed KV cache (priming window) to accept traffic within a capped RTO (target 90s switchover for core routes).
Priming window: prime top 5 token prefixes and top-10 recent conversation kernels per customer for stateful routes; rest of the cache fills on demand.
Consistency model: eventual for KV cache; traffic cutover must accept a quality delta agreement documented per route.

Traffic cutover steps: 1) mark destination routes in warm region as accept-ready, 2) enable controlled % traffic diversion (canary 1%, 5%, 25%), 3) monitor SLI delta and increase if safe, 4) revoke source region after verification.

Standby flavoring: warm-standby variants may run quantized or smaller models; this must be encoded in the SLO manifest under "variant_compatibility" and route owners must declare acceptable quality downgrade ranges.
Operational guardrails: automatic cutover only if KV-cache hit rate in standby > 30% within first 10 minutes and tail-quality SLI delta < declared threshold.
circuit_breaker_matrix: Tier 0 (Protective): Temporary soft-shed requests when queue latency > 800ms. Action: defer non-idempotent background calls and apply lightweight admission control. No customer-visible rejects for Gold-tier.
Tier 1 (Preemptive): When 5m availability drop >0.5% or 7d burn-rate >8x: reject Bronze-tier routes; enable 10% traffic diversion to warm-standby for Silver-tier.
Tier 2 (Escalation): When 5m availability drop >1.5% or sustained 7d burn-rate >16x: reject Silver-tier and escalate to regional failover for Gold; notify SRE on-call and open incident bridge.

Tier 3 (Emergency): If control-plane health impacted or control-plane anomalies detected: apply global protective throttle, route low-priority customers to best-effort queue, and engage Incident Commander.
State transitions include hysteresis windows to prevent flip-flop: once a tier enters, minimum hold is 15 minutes except manual override.
load_shedding_priorities: Priority 0: System-critical control-plane and telemetry ingestion (never shed automatically).
Priority 1 (Gold): SLA-backed enterprise customers pinned to dedicated capacity (shed only in extreme emergency and after manual approval).
Priority 2 (Silver): Standard paid customers with SLO bands; eligible for weighted diversion to warm-standby and circuit-breaker preemption.
Priority 3 (Bronze): Free-tier or best-effort customers; first to be evicted under Tier 1 circuit-breaker.
Eviction ordering within a priority: long-running batch routes -> non-interactive embedding bulk -> chat-style low-activity sessions -> interactive conversational sessions last.
observability: Dashboards required: per-route SLO overview (30d), short-term burn-rate (7d & 1h), top-k contributing reasons for errors (kernel OOM, overloaded GPU, model decode failures), KV cache heatmap.
Alerts: immediate P1 alert for 5m availability drop >1% for Gold routes; burn-rate early-warning when 7d burn-rate >4x expected.
Tracing: token-level tracing to attribute latency to kernel, compilation, queueing, or network. Must be sampled at 1% for production traffic and 10% for canaries.
Logs: structured error codes for automated aggregation (ERR_KERNEL_OOM, ERR_KV_MISS_COLD, ERR_COMPILATION_TIMEOUT, ERR_DEPLOY_CONFLICT).
rollout_checklist: Update SLO manifest schema (RFC link) and commit PR to infra-slos repo.
Add automated validation for SLI metrics in telemetry pipelines (unit tests + integration test against synthetic traffic).
Create canary: run warm-standby priming job in staging with real recent convo seeds; verify priming window behavior.
Run canaries for 48h with traffic shadowing and do rollback criteria: any tail-quality regression >2% or p95 latency regress >30%.
Coordinate with Console team for new dashboards and with Solutions for tenant impact communication.
Post-deploy: 7-day monitoring and a retro if any route crosses 25% of its 30d error budget in that period.
